original_test_intent: Verify that a defined CRPS internal fan-failure condition is saved in the PSU blackbox with the expected event identity and thermal/protection timeline.
original_method: A qualified operator applies a vendor-approved fan-fault simulation to the identified PSU under an approved load and thermal envelope, with independent tachometer/temperature monitoring and immediate cooling restoration. The raw blackbox event is extracted and correlated afterward.
manual_activity: A qualified engineer must establish and supervise any fan disconnection/simulation fixture and restore cooling. Agent monitoring and blackbox correlation are possible only after the specific safe method is approved.
required_inputs: PSU model/firmware and exact internal fan/tach channel
Vendor-approved fault method, load, duration, thermal/tach limits and expected protection behavior
Fixture/service procedure, independent temperature/tach monitoring and emergency cooling/cutoff
Blackbox tool/schema and expected fan-failure record fields
Operator, inspection/recovery plan and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Do not obstruct, unplug, damage or command the fan through an undocumented interface.
Do not infer that an AC event or workload throttle is a fan-failure equivalent.
Validate independent thermal/tach monitoring and immediate cooling restoration; preserve baseline logs.
Stop for limit approach, abnormal noise, smoke, output/protection anomaly or management loss.
No automatic reinjection, retry, reset or power cycle.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the approved method and capture permitted baseline telemetry.
After operator action, collect tach/temperature/load timeline and raw blackbox export.
Correlate event fields, protection behavior and cooling recovery.
Do not manipulate the fan or issue the formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Define/approve and perform the fan-fault mechanism within the thermal envelope.
Restore cooling and inspect/recover the PSU/load.
Provide inaccessible blackbox evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It safely refuses automation but is not a reproducible test command; its generic physical/AC language cannot select a fan-fault mechanism and its blackbox-access assumption is unsupported.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the vendor-approved fan-fault fixture/service SOP and blackbox extractor after the exact fan, thermal envelope and record contract are defined.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Attended Time 5 and Machine Time 5 remain source facts; no fault duration is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Define one non-destructive fan-failure simulation where possible, synchronize tach/temperature/load data, execute once under operator control, restore cooling immediately, and correlate the raw blackbox record.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the specified PSU/fan channel, load and approved fixture.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record PSU/BMC firmware, fixture/monitor versions/calibration and blackbox schema/tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project/vendor fan-fault, thermal and blackbox documentation must be supplied; no method is invented.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the fault channel, thermal envelope and recovery measurable while retaining blackbox verification.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A simulated tach loss may not cover a mechanically stalled rotor or airflow-loss signature unless vendor equivalence is documented.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Fan identity, fault method, load, duration, thermal/tach limits, expected record and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: PSU internal cooling loss can cause fast local temperature rise not visible in platform sensors.

project_override_considerations: A project may use a vendor simulation instead of mechanical obstruction if equivalence to the blackbox fan-fault path is documented. Record whether coverage is tach loss, rotor stall or airflow loss; do not generalize across them.
expected_evidence: Approved fan/channel/fault method, load, thermal envelope, monitoring and safety checklist
Operator record plus synchronized tach/temperature/load and restoration timeline
Raw blackbox export with schema/tool version and expected fan-fault fields
Preserved platform logs and verified cooling/PSU/load recovery

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item and procedure align on blackbox capture of a fan-failure status. The missing failure mechanism and limits are severe underspecification, not contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Different fan-fault mechanisms exercise different paths and thermal risks. With no safe mechanism, envelope or expected record, execution cannot proceed without inventing the test.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agree the agent must not induce the fault; reject its generic AC/throttle alternatives and unsupported access assertion.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with BLOCKED and its fan-specific thermal/monitoring/record/recovery gates.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates tach, stall and airflow coverage and identifies which post-stimulus work can later be automated.

review_improvement: This review prevents unsafe inference of obstruction/unplugging, defines channel-specific thermal evidence and avoids conflating this PSU-blackbox case with other library fan-failure variants.
independent_technical_reasoning: The named fault is clear at a high level but not operationally: stopping drive, losing tach and blocking airflow are materially different. Since choosing one changes safety and coverage, the missing method is a genuine blocker rather than a normal parameter gap.
